packageRules.description: Give npm releases three days before proposing them

Every major update waits for approval on the Dependency Dashboard, toolchain majors included: pnpm (packageManager in package.json) and Node (node-version in the workflows). A major can drop a platform or change defaults, so someone reads its notes before a PR opens

An update that is breaking by its versioning's own rules waits too, for the same reason. Renovate calls a Cargo 0.x minor, such as libloading 0.7 to 0.9, a minor, so the major rule misses it; matchIsBreaking does not

Every Rust release (rust-toolchain.toml) waits for approval. Renovate keeps Rust's major at 1, so the major rule never holds one, yet a release can add clippy lints that fail -D warnings or raise platform minimums; someone reads its notes before a PR opens

Runner labels are pinned and moved by hand, every job in one change, with branch protection's required checks (roadmap §2, CI hygiene). Renovate reads only literal runs-on labels, not ci.yml's os matrix, so its PRs would split jobs across OS releases
Tauri crates and npm packages move together (xtask check enforces parity; xtask pins tauri-utils to tauri's)

The WebDriver test stack moves together, in one branch even for a major, and waits for approval on the Dependency Dashboard. The tauri-plugin-wdio-webdriver git pin (app/src-tauri/Cargo.toml) is matched by its repository URL: matchPackageNames matches packageName, which for a Cargo git dependency is the URL, not the crate name. Whoever approves re-keys or drops the @wdio/tauri-service patch in pnpm-workspace.yaml, which is keyed to 1.4.0 and follows that pin, in the same branch
TypeScript 7 is not supported by svelte-check yet (ADR 0001)
